summary.whatChanges: tRPC's `httpLink` and `httpBatchLink` now abort the underlying fetch when a subscription is unsubscribed before the request settles. Each operation gets its own AbortController raced with the caller's signal, and the teardown function aborts it unless the request already completed. Tests cover both links.
behaviorChanges: Unsubscribing a query/mutation made through httpLink cancels the in-flight fetch instead of leaving it running
Unsubscribing through httpBatchLink aborts that operation's signal, cancelling the batched fetch request
The fetch signal's abort reason is an AbortError after unsubscribe
Teardown after the request already resolved or rejected no longer triggers an abort
risks: In httpBatchLink, aborting one operation's signal may cancel the whole shared batch request for other operations, depending on dataLoader's signal-merging behavior
Requests that previously completed in the background after unsubscribe (e.g. warming a cache or non-idempotent mutations) are now cancelled mid-flight
The isDone flag is set inside promise callbacks, so a synchronous unsubscribe immediately after settlement could still race and abort
raceAbortSignals allocates a listener/controller per operation; no visible cleanup of the raced signal on completion
